about.lead: Stefan Bogdanovic · owner and main contact · Zurich
body: I know day-to-day operations from hotel and front-desk environments and the everyday user, access and system questions small businesses face.

BIT supports small businesses without in-house IT with user accounts, Microsoft 365, access and recurring workplace issues. I work as an operational contact — not as a general IT expert for every issue, and not as an expert team.
I remain the contractual counterparty. As a sole proprietorship I am your contact for intake, written scope, follow-up and billing.
Working languages for this Swiss IT site: German and English. Other languages by agreement or with external language support.

faq.meta_description: Common questions about BIT’s scope, audience and way of working.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions

items.q: Is BIT an in-house IT department?
items.a: No. BIT takes structured ownership of clearly scoped user, access and workplace requests, documents them and follows them through. Scope is agreed in writing first.
Smaller companies with about 5–50 employees, mostly on Windows and Microsoft 365, without a dedicated IT role — Zurich and remote across Switzerland.

items.q: Can every IT problem be covered?
items.a: No. BIT takes on clearly scoped user, access and workplace tasks within a written scope. Complex infrastructure, vendor-dependent or specialist topics are not automatically included and are reviewed before work starts.

items.q: Does BIT only work with hotels?
items.a: No. Hotels and front desk are one experience example. The offer is aimed at smaller Swiss companies without in-house IT.
It depends on the case and the written agreement. Where a task sits outside my own scope, I check first whether a suitable external specialist can be involved.
Permission and access changes only happen after documented approval and within the written scope.

items.q: Are there fixed packages or prices?
items.a: There are guideline rates (working time CHF 120 per hour). The IT basics check is a fixed-price entry from CHF 190 with a written finding and priorities. Most requests are handled remotely. If an on-site appointment is required, it is agreed in advance and listed separately in the quote — Zurich area, with no hidden travel flat fee. Prices become binding only after written review of scope.

examples_page.title: How an engagement with BIT can run
examples_page.lead: The following examples are illustrative sample cases, not client references. They show how BIT structures clearly scoped user, access and workplace tasks — from approval through to documented close-out.

cases.title: Sample: employee departure
cases.situation: Someone is leaving the company. It is unclear which accounts, mailboxes and access rights remain active and who may approve deactivation.
required: Whether devices or shared mailboxes are involved
steps: Capture starting point and affected systems
Handle approved changes within the agreed scope or coordinate technical execution with the responsible specialist function.
Document close-out plus open points and risks
cases.approvals: Written approval from the responsible manager before any access change.
cases.result: Documented overview of handled access, confirmation of deactivation steps and a list of open points.

cases.title: Sample: new employee starts on Monday
cases.situation: A new employee should start ready to work. Required access, licences and devices are not yet clearly assembled.
steps: Arrange setup of approved accounts, rights and licences and document them.
cases.approvals: Approval for accounts, rights and any licences before setup.
cases.result: Checklist of set-up access, known limitations and next steps if anything is missing.

cases.title: Sample: Outlook does not work at a workstation
cases.situation: Outlook is unusable at a workstation. It is unclear whether only this workstation or further users are affected, and whether the cause sits with the account, the device or the service.
required: Exact error message or observed behaviour
Since when the issue has existed
Recent changes to account, device or software
steps: Narrow whether account, device or service is affected
Handle within the confirmed scope or coordinate with the responsible specialist function
Document the outcome and open points
cases.approvals: Access to the affected workstation only by agreement with the responsible person.
cases.result: Documented root-cause narrowing, measures taken or coordinated, and a list of open points.
